# Getting Started ## Welcome to the Dutchie Point of Sale API The Dutchie Point of Sale API provides comprehensive access to your retail cannabis data, enabling seamless integration with your business systems. ### Key Features - **Product Management** — Access and update product catalogs - **Customer Data** — Manage customer information and relationships - **Transaction History** — Retrieve detailed sales and payment data - **Inventory Tracking** — Monitor stock levels and movements - **Reporting & Analytics** — Generate business insights and compliance reports ### Common Use Cases - **E-commerce Integration** — Sync products and inventory with online stores - **Business Intelligence** — Extract data for analytics and reporting tools - **Customer Relationship Management** — Integrate customer data with CRM systems - **Compliance Reporting** — Generate required regulatory reports - **Multi-location Management** — Centralize data across multiple store locations ## Quick Start Guide Get up and running with the Dutchie API in just 5 minutes. ### Step 1: Get Your API Keys Follow the [API key request process](https://support.dutchie.com/hc/en-us/articles/27660267271187-Dutchie-POS-API-key-request-process-for-third-party-integrations) to get started. When requesting keys, be specific about: - **Your use case** — What business problem are you solving? - **Required data** — What information do you need to access? - **Operations needed** — Do you need read-only or read-write access? - **Specific endpoints** — Which API endpoints will you be calling? Once approved, you'll receive: - A **Location Key** for each dispensary location you need to access - An **Integrator Key** that identifies your integration (shared across locations) — currently optional but will be required in a future release > [!warning] > Location Keys are vendor-specific. A key issued for one vendor integration will not work for another vendor's data access. ### Step 2: Authentication The API uses **HTTP Basic Authentication**. Your keys map to the standard Basic Auth fields: | Credential | Basic Auth Field | Description | |---|---|---| | **Location Key** | Username | Identifies the specific dispensary location. Required on every request. | | **Integrator Key** | Password | Identifies the integration partner. Currently optional; will be required in a future release. | If you do not yet have an Integrator Key, leave the password empty. **With both keys (recommended):** ``` Authorization: Basic {base64(location_key:integrator_key)} ``` **With Location Key only:** ``` Authorization: Basic {base64(location_key:)} ``` **Manual Encoding Example:** ```bash # With both keys: # Location Key: loc_abc123 Integrator Key: int_xyz789 # Encode "loc_abc123:int_xyz789" # Result: bG9jX2FiYzEyMzppbnRfeHl6Nzg5 Authorization: Basic bG9jX2FiYzEyMzppbnRfeHl6Nzg5 # With Location Key only: # Encode "loc_abc123:" # Result: bG9jX2FiYzEyMzo= Authorization: Basic bG9jX2FiYzEyMzo= ``` > [!tip] > Most HTTP clients handle Basic Auth encoding automatically when you provide the username and password fields. **Security Best Practices:** - **Environment Variables** — Store keys in environment variables, not in code - **Secure Configuration** — Use secure configuration management systems - **Never Commit Keys** — Add API keys to your `.gitignore` file - **Access Control** — Limit key access to necessary personnel only ### Step 3: Test Your Authentication Use the `/whoami` endpoint to verify your keys are working and see which location they access: ```bash # With both keys curl -X GET "https://api.pos.dutchie.com/whoami" \ -u "your_location_key:your_integrator_key" \ -H "Accept: application/json" # With Location Key only curl -X GET "https://api.pos.dutchie.com/whoami" \ -u "your_location_key:" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` **Expected Responses:** - **200 OK** — Authentication successful, returns location information - **401 Unauthorized** — Invalid or missing Location Key (or invalid Integrator Key once enforcement begins) - **403 Forbidden** — Valid keys but insufficient permissions ### Step 4: Base URL & Endpoints All API requests are made to: `https://api.pos.dutchie.com` **Common Endpoints:** - `GET /products` — Retrieve all products *(requires Inventory permission)* - `GET /customer/customers` — Retrieve all customers *(requires Customer permission)* - `GET /reporting/register-transactions` — Get transaction data *(requires Reporting permission)* - `GET /reporting/inventory` — Get current inventory levels *(requires Reporting permission)* - `GET /whoami` — Verify your keys and get location info *(no special permissions needed)* > [!note] > Each endpoint requires specific permission scopes. See [Permissions & Scopes](#description/permissions--scopes) for complete details. ### Step 5: Your First API Call Test your setup by fetching products: **cURL:** ```bash # With both keys (recommended) curl -X GET "https://api.pos.dutchie.com/products" \ -u "your_location_key:your_integrator_key" \ -H "Accept: application/json" # Without an Integrator Key curl -X GET "https://api.pos.dutchie.com/products" \ -u "your_location_key" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` **JavaScript (Fetch API):** ```javascript const locationKey = 'your_location_key'; const integratorKey = 'your_integrator_key'; // leave as '' if you don't have one yet const encodedKey = typeof btoa !== 'undefined' ? btoa(locationKey + ':' + integratorKey) : Buffer.from(locationKey + ':' + integratorKey).toString('base64'); async function getProducts() { const response = await fetch('https://api.pos.dutchie.com/products', { method: 'GET', headers: { 'Authorization': `Basic ${encodedKey}`, 'Accept': 'application/json' } }); if (!response.ok) { throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`); } return await response.json(); } ``` ### Step 6: Understanding API Responses All successful responses return data directly as JSON (no wrapper structure): ```json // GET /products returns an array directly [ { "productId": 12345, "name": "Product Name", "price": 29.99 } ] // GET /whoami returns an object directly { "locationName": "Store Name", "address": "123 Main St", "lspName": "Company Name" } ``` # API Concepts ## Integration Design This API is designed for **data synchronization**, not live transactional queries. Build your integrations accordingly. ### Recommended Patterns - **Periodic Data Sync** — Pull data at regular intervals (hourly, daily) to keep your systems updated - **Batch Processing** — Process multiple records together rather than making individual calls - **Offline-First Architecture** — Store data locally and sync periodically rather than querying live - **[Incremental Updates](#description/incremental-sync)** — Use date/time filters to pull only changed data since your last sync - **Caching Strategy** — Cache API responses and refresh them based on your business needs ### Patterns to Avoid - **Real-time Queries** — Don't query the API for every user action or page load - **Excessive Polling** — Avoid calling endpoints more frequently than your business logic requires - **Live Customer Lookups** — Don't query customer data in real-time during checkout processes - **Transaction-by-transaction Sync** — Avoid individual API calls for each business transaction - **Synchronous Dependencies** — Don't make your user experience dependent on live API response times ### Integration Architecture ``` 1. Pull data from Dutchie API → Local database/cache 2. Serve your application from local data 3. Sync changes back to local data periodically 4. Handle API rate limits and retries gracefully ``` ### Data Freshness API data is updated as transactions occur in your point of sale system. Most endpoints reflect changes within a few minutes. While the system processes updates quickly, you should expect a small delay (typically 1–5 minutes) rather than completely real-time data. ## Permissions & Scopes The Dutchie Point of Sale API uses **role-based permissions** to control access to different types of data and operations. Each Location Key is granted specific permission scopes based on your integration needs. > [!note] > Location Keys are issued with specific permission scopes. You only get access to endpoints that match your granted permissions. [Contact Dutchie Support](https://support.dutchie.com/hc/en-us/articles/27660267271187-Dutchie-POS-API-key-request-process-for-third-party-integrations) to request additional permissions if needed. ### Permission Scopes Reference | Scope | Endpoints | |---|---| | `Reporting` | `GET /reporting/inventory`
`GET /reporting/register-transactions` | | `Customer` | `GET /customer/by-external-id`
`GET /customer/customers`
`GET /customer/customers-paginated`
`GET /customer/referral-sources`
`POST /customer/customer`
`POST /customer/customerLookup`
`POST /customer/search` | | `Inventory` | `GET /products`
`GET /strains`
`GET /tag/*`
`POST /products` | | `PreOrder` | `POST /transaction/*` | | `Vendor` | `GET /vendor/*` | | `CultivationWrite` | `POST /waste/HarvestWaste`
`POST /waste/PlantWaste` | | `Room` | `GET /room/*`
`GET /table/*` | | `Reporting,Deliveries` | `GET /vehicles` *(requires either scope)* | | *No scope required* | `GET /brand`
`GET /customer/customer-types`
`GET /reference/*`
`GET /regulatory-category`
`GET /sizes`
`GET /terminals`
`GET /whoami` | ## Rate Limits The Dutchie Point of Sale API implements fair usage policies to ensure optimal performance for all users. Our rate limits are designed to accommodate normal business operations while preventing abuse. ### Rate Limit Structure Rate limits are applied per-endpoint and per-Location-Key, measured in requests per minute. The API uses a baseline rate limit with endpoint-specific variations based on resource intensity and usage patterns. **Rate Limit Tiers:** | Endpoint Category | Rate Limit | Examples | Reasoning | |---|---|---|---| | **Standard Endpoints** | `120/min` | GET /products, GET /customers | Baseline rate for most operations | | **High-Traffic Endpoints** | `200/min` | GET /inventory, GET /whoami | Frequently accessed, optimized data | | **Resource-Intensive** | `60/min` | Reporting endpoints | Complex queries, larger datasets | | **Bulk Operations** | `10/min` | Batch imports, bulk updates | High server resource usage | > [!note] > The standard rate limit is **120 requests per minute** per Location Key. Most endpoints use this baseline unless specifically configured otherwise for performance reasons. ### Finding Endpoint Rate Limits Each endpoint's specific rate limit is documented in its API reference documentation. Look for: - **Endpoint Documentation** — Check the specific endpoint's documentation for its rate limit - **API Explorer** — Rate limits are shown in the interactive API documentation - **Default Assumption** — If no specific rate limit is mentioned, assume the baseline 120/min > [!warning] > Rate limits may be adjusted based on system performance and usage patterns. Always refer to the current endpoint documentation for the most up-to-date limits. ### Rate Limit Exceeded When you exceed the rate limit, the API returns a `429 Too Many Requests` response: ```http HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests Content-Type: application/json { "Message": "Too many requests - only 120 per minute allowed", "TraceId": "0HM2AFJV13H6F:00000001" } ``` **Handling Rate Limits:** - **Implement exponential backoff** — Gradually increase wait times for repeated failures - **Monitor request patterns** — Track your request frequency to avoid hitting limits - **Cache responses** — Reduce API calls by caching frequently accessed data - **Use batch operations** — Prefer bulk endpoints when available ### Staying Within Limits - **Spread requests evenly** — Avoid bursting all requests at the top of each minute - **Cache responses** — Reduce API calls by caching frequently accessed data locally - **Retry with backoff** — On 429 responses, wait with exponential backoff before retrying - **Monitor usage** — Track your request frequency and set alerts for approaching limits ### Capacity Planning Plan your integration based on the baseline 120 requests/minute (2 requests/second) rate limit: - **Hourly Capacity** — 7,200 requests per hour (120 × 60) - **Daily Capacity** — 172,800 requests per day (120 × 60 × 24) - **Safety Margin** — Plan for 80% of capacity (96 requests/minute) to handle spikes - **Burst Prevention** — Spread requests evenly rather than in bursts > [!tip] > **Planning Example:** If you need to sync 1,000 customers daily, that's ~42 API calls per hour, well within the 7,200/hour capacity. You can safely sync every 5 minutes during business hours. See [Incremental Sync](#description/incremental-sync) for recommended sync frequencies by data type. ## Pagination The Dutchie Point of Sale API uses different pagination strategies depending on the endpoint. Most endpoints return complete datasets, while specific endpoints offer pagination for large collections. ### Pagination Overview **Default Behavior** — Most API endpoints return **all available data** in a single response. This approach is optimized for typical business operations where complete datasets are needed for synchronization. **When Pagination is Used** — Pagination is available for endpoints that may return very large datasets, such as: - Customer records (thousands of customers) - Historical transaction data - Loyalty program transactions ### Pagination Methods | Endpoint | Pagination Type | Parameters | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `GET /customer/customers` | None | — | Returns all customers | | `GET /customer/customers-paginated` | Page-based | PageNumber, PageSize | Large customer datasets | | `GET /products` | None | — | Returns all products | | `GET /reporting/register-transactions` | None | Date range | Filtered by date range | ### Page-Based Pagination Used by endpoints like `/customer/customers-paginated` for straightforward page navigation. **Request Parameters:** - `PageNumber` — Page to retrieve (starts at 0) - `PageSize` — Number of records per page (max 100) **Example Request:** ``` GET /customer/customers-paginated?PageNumber=0&PageSize=50 ``` **Example Response:** ```json [ { "customerID": 12345, "firstName": "John", "lastName": "Doe" }, { "customerID": 12346, "firstName": "Jane", "lastName": "Smith" } ] ``` > [!note] > The customers-paginated endpoint returns a direct array. Check the array length against your PageSize to determine if there are more pages. **Navigation Pattern:** 1. Start with `PageNumber=0` 2. Check if returned array length equals `PageSize` 3. If array length < PageSize, you've reached the last page 4. If array length = PageSize, there may be more pages 5. Increment `PageNumber` and continue ### Cursor-Based Pagination Used by select endpoints for efficient traversal of large, time-ordered datasets. **Request Parameters:** - `pageKey` — Token for the next page (omit for first page) - `maxPageSize` — Number of records per page (max varies by endpoint) **Example First Request:** ``` GET /example-endpoint?maxPageSize=100 ``` **Example Response:** ```json { "items": [ { "lspId": 123, "locId": 456, "customerId": 789, "transactionType": "Earned", "transactionDateUtc": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z", "points": 25.0, "adjustmentReason": null, "comment": "Purchase points", "registerTransactionId": 98765 } ], "pageSize": 100, "haveMoreData": true, "nextPageKey": "offset:100" } ``` **Next Page Request:** ``` GET /example-endpoint?pageKey=offset:100&maxPageSize=100 ``` > [!tip] > Cursor-based pagination handles real-time data changes better than page-based pagination, ensuring you don't miss records or see duplicates. ### Best Practices **Choose the Right Approach:** - **Complete Sync** — Use non-paginated endpoints for full data synchronization - **Large Datasets** — Use paginated endpoints when working with thousands of records - **Memory Management** — Process paginated data in chunks to avoid memory issues **Error Handling:** - **Invalid Page Numbers** — Handle out-of-range page requests gracefully - **Expired Cursors** — Restart from the beginning if cursor tokens expire - **Network Failures** — Implement retry logic for failed page requests **Performance Optimization:** - **Page Size** — Use appropriate page sizes (50–100 for most use cases) - **Parallel Processing** — Process multiple pages concurrently when possible - **Incremental Updates** — Combine pagination with date filters for efficiency > [!warning] > Paginated requests count against your [rate limits](#description/rate-limits). Monitor your usage when processing large datasets. ### Working with Non-Paginated Endpoints Most Dutchie API endpoints return complete datasets optimized for business operations: - **Products** — Complete catalog (typically 100–500 items) - **Customers** — All customers (use paginated version for large stores) - **Transactions** — Filtered by date range to manage size - **Inventory** — Current levels for all products **Date Range Filtering** — Many endpoints use date ranges instead of pagination to manage response size: ``` GET /reporting/register-transactions?fromLastModifiedDateUTC=2024-01-01T00:00:00Z&toLastModifiedDateUTC=2024-01-31T23:59:59Z ``` > [!tip] > Start with non-paginated endpoints for simplicity, then switch to paginated versions if you encounter performance issues with large datasets. ### Implementation Examples **Page-Based Loop (JavaScript):** ```javascript async function getAllCustomers() { let allCustomers = []; let currentPage = 1; let hasMoreData = true; const pageSize = 100; while (hasMoreData) { const response = await fetch( `/customer/customers-paginated?PageNumber=${currentPage}&PageSize=${pageSize}` ); const customers = await response.json(); allCustomers.push(...customers); hasMoreData = customers.length === pageSize; currentPage++; } return allCustomers; } ``` **Cursor-Based Loop (JavaScript):** ```javascript async function getAllLoyaltyTransactions() { let allTransactions = []; let nextPageKey = null; do { const url = nextPageKey ? `/example-endpoint?pageKey=${nextPageKey}&maxPageSize=100` : '/example-endpoint?maxPageSize=100'; const response = await fetch(url); const data = await response.json(); allTransactions.push(...data.items); nextPageKey = data.haveMoreData ? data.nextPageKey : null; } while (nextPageKey); return allTransactions; } ``` ## Incremental Sync Incremental synchronization allows you to efficiently update your local data by retrieving only records that have changed since your last sync. This approach minimizes API calls, reduces bandwidth usage, and improves performance. ### Why Use Incremental Sync? - **Reduced API Calls** — Only fetch data that has actually changed - **Lower Bandwidth** — Transfer minimal data over the network - **Faster Updates** — Shorter sync times for better user experience - **Rate Limit Efficiency** — Conserve your [API rate limits](#description/rate-limits) - **Real-time Feel** — More frequent updates without performance impact **When to Use:** - Regular data synchronization (every few minutes/hours) - Large datasets that change infrequently - Real-time or near-real-time integrations - Mobile applications with bandwidth constraints ### Supported Endpoints | Endpoint | Modified Date Parameter | Typical Update Frequency | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `GET /products` | `fromLastModifiedDateUTC` | Low (hours/days) | Product catalog changes | | `GET /customer/customers` | `fromLastModifiedDateUTC` | Medium (minutes/hours) | Customer profile updates | | `GET /reporting/inventory` | *None (current snapshot only)* | Medium (minutes/hours) | Current inventory levels | | `GET /reporting/register-transactions` | `fromLastModifiedDateUTC` / `toLastModifiedDateUTC` | High (real-time) | Transaction history by date range | ### Date-Based Filtering Most endpoints support date-based filtering using ISO 8601 formatted timestamps in UTC. **Common Parameters:** - `fromLastModifiedDateUTC` — Returns records modified after this timestamp - `toLastModifiedDateUTC` — Returns records modified before this timestamp (for date range filtering) **Example Request:** ``` GET /products?fromLastModifiedDateUTC=2024-01-15T10:30:00Z ``` **Date Format:** - **Format:** ISO 8601 UTC timestamp - **Example:** `2024-01-15T10:30:00Z` - **Timezone:** Always UTC (indicated by `Z`) > [!note] > All timestamps in the API are in UTC. Convert your local timestamps to UTC before making requests. ### Implementation Strategy **Step 1 — Initial Full Sync:** Start with a complete data sync to establish your baseline: ```javascript // Initial sync — get all products const products = await fetch('/products'); // Store the current timestamp for next sync const lastSyncTime = new Date().toISOString(); ``` **Step 2 — Store Last Sync Timestamp:** - Store timestamp in your database - Use the timestamp from when sync *started* (not when it finished) - Only update stored timestamp after successful completion **Step 3 — Incremental Updates:** ```javascript // Incremental sync const updated = await fetch( `/products?fromLastModifiedDateUTC=${lastSyncTime}` ); // Process updates, then update timestamp const newSyncTime = new Date().toISOString(); ``` **Step 4 — Handle Edge Cases:** - **Clock Skew** — Subtract a small buffer (30–60 seconds) from your timestamp - **Failed Syncs** — Don't update stored timestamp on failures - **Data Gaps** — Implement periodic full syncs as backup ### Implementation Example ```javascript class IncrementalSync { constructor(apiClient, storage) { this.api = apiClient; this.storage = storage; } async syncProducts() { const lastSync = await this.storage.getLastSync('products'); const syncStartTime = new Date().toISOString(); try { const params = lastSync ? { fromLastModifiedDateUTC: lastSync } : {}; const response = await this.api.get('/products', { params }); await this.processProductUpdates(response.data); // Update last sync time only on success await this.storage.setLastSync('products', syncStartTime); return { success: true, updatedCount: response.data.length, isIncremental: !!lastSync }; } catch (error) { // Don't update lastSync timestamp on failure throw error; } } async processProductUpdates(products) { for (const product of products) { await this.storage.upsertProduct(product); } } } ``` **Sync Scheduler:** ```javascript const syncSchedule = { products: 3600000, // 1 hour (low change frequency) customers: 300000, // 5 minutes (medium change frequency) inventory: 60000, // 1 minute (high change frequency) transactions: 30000 // 30 seconds (real-time needs) }; Object.entries(syncSchedule).forEach(([endpoint, interval]) => { setInterval(async () => { try { await syncManager.sync(endpoint); } catch (error) { console.error(`${endpoint} sync failed:`, error); } }, interval); }); ``` ### Important Considerations **Clock Synchronization** — Server and client clocks may not be perfectly synchronized: - **Buffer Time** — Subtract 30–60 seconds from your last sync timestamp - **Server Response Headers** — Use server timestamps when available - **NTP Sync** — Keep your systems synchronized with NTP > [!warning] > If your clock is 30 seconds ahead of the server, you might miss updates that occur in that 30-second window. **Handling Deletions:** - **Soft Deletes** — Some endpoints mark records as inactive rather than deleting - **Periodic Full Syncs** — Run complete syncs periodically to detect removals - **Business Logic** — Implement your own deletion detection logic **Error Recovery:** - **Failed Requests** — Don't advance your last sync timestamp - **Partial Failures** — Consider the sync failed if any critical step fails - **Retry Logic** — Implement exponential backoff for temporary failures - **Fallback to Full Sync** — Use full sync as recovery mechanism ### Sync Frequency Guidelines - **Products** — Every 1–4 hours (low change frequency) - **Customers** — Every 5–15 minutes (medium change frequency) - **Inventory** — Every 1–5 minutes (high change frequency) - **Transactions** — Every 30 seconds to 2 minutes (real-time needs) > [!tip] > Start with longer sync intervals and gradually decrease them based on your actual business needs and rate limit capacity. ## Idempotency Checks Prevent duplicate operations with guaranteed request deduplication. When enabled, the system guarantees that identical requests will successfully complete at most once, regardless of network issues, client retries, or other circumstances that might cause duplicate submissions. This applies to creating customers and processing pre-orders where duplicate execution could cause business problems. For 400-type validation errors, you can correct your request and retry without needing to change the IdempotencyKey. ### How Idempotency Works The idempotency system uses a combination of two identifiers: 1. **`ConsumerKey` Header** — Identifies the client/integrator making the request 2. **`IdempotencyKey` Field** — Unique identifier for the specific operation Together, these create a unique fingerprint for each request. If the same combination is seen again, the system will return the original response without re-executing the operation. > [!note] > Idempotency is opt-in. Both values must be provided to enable idempotency checking. Missing either value simply disables the feature without causing errors. ### Implementation Requirements **ConsumerKey Header (Optional):** ``` ConsumerKey: {guid} ``` - **Format:** Valid GUID (e.g., `123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000`) - **Purpose:** Identifies your application/integration - **Scope:** Should be consistent for the entity you're wanting idempotent actions against **IdempotencyKey Request Field (Optional):** - **Maximum Length:** 36 characters - **Format:** Any string, but GUIDs recommended for uniqueness - **Scope:** Must be unique per ConsumerKey+Location Key combination you want to protect - **Recommendation:** Generate a new UUID for each distinct operation ### Idempotency Behavior **When Both Values Are Present:** *First Request:* - System checks if ConsumerKey + IdempotencyKey combination exists - If not found, the operation proceeds normally - Upon successful completion, the combination of ConsumerKey + Location Key + IdempotencyKey is stored with the response - Upon error, the request is unprocessed and may be retried (you may change the request body without changing the idempotency key) - Normal response is returned *Duplicate Request:* - System finds existing ConsumerKey + Location Key + IdempotencyKey combination - Operation is **NOT** executed again - Original stored response is returned - No side effects occur (no database changes, no external calls) **When Values Are Missing:** - **Missing ConsumerKey or IdempotencyKey** — System ignores idempotency - **Operation proceeds normally** — No idempotency checking is performed - **No errors thrown** — Missing values do not cause validation failures **Response Codes:** - **200 OK** — Operation completed (either first time, idempotent repeat, or non-idempotent) - **500 Internal Server Error** — May occur with invalid values that cause casting or truncation issues ### Endpoints Supporting Idempotency **Customer Management:** - **POST /customer/customer** — Create new customers with duplicate prevention - Do **not** use your internally generated customer ID when *editing* a customer, as that would discard edits. Instead, use an identifier of the change itself. Consider generating a GUID, or not passing in an idempotency key at all as repeat edit operations are inherently idempotent and safe. **Pre-Order Management:** - **POST /preorder/submit** — Create pre-orders with duplicate prevention > [!warning] > Only endpoints explicitly documented as supporting idempotency will honor the `ConsumerKey` header and `IdempotencyKey` field. Other endpoints will ignore these values. ### Examples **Creating a Customer:** ```http POST /customer/customer ConsumerKey: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000 Content-Type: application/json { "IdempotencyKey": "customer-1234", "FirstName": "John", "LastName": "Doe", "Email": "john.doe@example.com" } ``` **Creating a Pre-Order:** ```http POST /preorder/submit ConsumerKey: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000 Content-Type: application/json { "IdempotencyKey": "preorder-1234", "CustomerId": 12345, "Items": [...] } ``` ### Best Practices **ConsumerKey Management:** - Use a single, consistent GUID for your entire application - Store the ConsumerKey securely in your application configuration - Do not share ConsumerKeys between different applications or environments **IdempotencyKey Generation:** - Generate a new UUID for each distinct business operation - When creating a preorder or customer, use your own internally generated and unique database key - Use deterministic generation based on operation context when appropriate - Avoid reusing keys unless you specifically want idempotent behavior **Error Handling:** - Include both `ConsumerKey` and `IdempotencyKey` when you want idempotency protection - Omit either value if you want to bypass idempotency checking - Handle potential 400 or 500 errors that may occur with malformed values - Implement retry logic that preserves the same `IdempotencyKey` for consistent deduplication ### Troubleshooting | Issue | Resolution | |---|---| | 500 Internal Server Error with idempotency values | Check that `ConsumerKey` is a valid GUID format and `IdempotencyKey` doesn't exceed 36 characters | | Unexpected duplicate prevention | Check if you're reusing `IdempotencyKey` values across different operations | | Operations not being deduplicated | Confirm the endpoint supports idempotency and both `ConsumerKey` and `IdempotencyKey` are provided | | Idempotency seems disabled | Verify both `ConsumerKey` header and `IdempotencyKey` field are present — missing either disables checking | ## Error Handling The Dutchie Point of Sale API uses standard HTTP status codes and provides detailed error messages to help you diagnose and resolve issues quickly. ### HTTP Status Codes **Success Codes (2xx):** | Code | Status | Description | When You'll See It | |---|---|---|---| | `200` | OK | Request succeeded | GET requests returning data successfully | | `201` | Created | Resource created successfully | POST requests that create new resources | | `204` | No Content | Request succeeded, no content returned | DELETE requests or updates with no response body | **Client Error Codes (4xx):** | Code | Status | Common Causes | How to Fix | |---|---|---|---| | `400` | Bad Request | Invalid request format, missing required fields | Check request body format and required parameters | | `401` | Unauthorized | Missing or invalid Location Key, or invalid Integrator Key | Verify your Location Key is correct and properly encoded. If you provide an Integrator Key, verify it as well. | | `403` | Forbidden | Valid keys but insufficient permissions | Contact support to verify your [permission scopes](#description/permissions--scopes) | | `404` | Not Found | Resource doesn't exist or incorrect endpoint | Check endpoint URL and resource ID | | `422` | Unprocessable Entity | Valid format but business logic validation failed | Review validation errors in response body | | `429` | Too Many Requests | [Rate limit](#description/rate-limits) exceeded | Implement exponential backoff and retry logic | **Server Error Codes (5xx):** | Code | Status | What It Means | What to Do | |---|---|---|---| | `500` | Internal Server Error | Unexpected server-side error or bug | Log error; contact support (do not retry) | | `502` | Bad Gateway | Gateway/proxy server issue | Retry with exponential backoff | | `503` | Service Unavailable | Service temporarily down for maintenance | Check status page; retry after specified time | ### Error Response Formats **Authentication Errors (401):** Authentication failures return an empty response body with HTTP 401 status. ```http HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized Content-Length: 0 ``` **Not Found Errors (404):** ```http HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found Content-Length: 0 ``` **Server Errors (500):** ```http HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error Content-Length: 0 ``` ### Validation Error Formats (400) The API uses **five distinct response formats** for validation errors, each optimized for different error scenarios. Clients should handle the specific response format for the endpoints they are calling. #### 1. Empty Response (void) Used for simple validation failures with binary success/failure states (e.g., plant operations, package operations). **How to Identify:** In the API documentation, look for **400 Bad Request** responses marked as `void`. ```http HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request Content-Length: 0 ``` #### 2. String Response Used for business rule violations requiring a single descriptive message (e.g., pre-order status validation, pricing calculations). **How to Identify:** Look for **400 Bad Request** responses with schema type `string`. ```http HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request "Please request fewer than 10000 customers at a time" ``` #### 3. BadRequestResponse (Simple Message) Used for business logic violations in a structured format (e.g., customer operations, product validation). **How to Identify:** Look for **400 Bad Request** responses with `BadRequestResponse` schema where `propertyErrors` is null. ```json { "message": "Customer is null or unparseable", "propertyErrors": null } ``` #### 4. BadRequestResponse (Field-Specific Errors) Used for form validation with multiple field-level errors (e.g., customer registration, multi-field validation). **How to Identify:** Look for **400 Bad Request** responses with `BadRequestResponse` schema with populated `propertyErrors`. ```json { "message": "Errors found. Check PropertyErrors.", "propertyErrors": [ { "propertyName": "Email", "propertyError": "Email address is required" }, { "propertyName": "DateOfBirth", "propertyError": "Date must be between 1800 and current date" } ] } ``` #### 5. ValidationResult Format Used for comprehensive validation with detailed metadata (e.g., driver management, vehicle management, delivery operations). **How to Identify:** Look for **400 Bad Request** responses with `ValidationResult` schema showing `isValid`, `errors`, and `ruleSetsExecuted` fields. ```json { "isValid": false, "errors": [ { "propertyName": "Email", "errorMessage": "Email address is required", "attemptedValue": "", "customState": null, "severity": 0, "errorCode": "NotEmptyValidator", "formattedMessagePlaceholderValues": { "PropertyName": "Email", "PropertyValue": "" } } ], "ruleSetsExecuted": [] } ``` ### Retry Logic Example ```javascript async function apiWithRetry(endpoint, options = {}, maxRetries = 3) { let lastError; for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) { try { return await callAPI(endpoint, options); } catch (error) { lastError = error; // Don't retry on client errors (4xx except 429) or 500 if ((error.status >= 400 && error.status < 500 && error.status !== 429) || error.status === 500) { throw error; } const delay = Math.min(1000 * Math.pow(2, attempt), 30000); if (attempt < maxRetries) { await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, delay)); } } } throw lastError; } ``` ### Error Handling Pattern ```javascript function handleAPIError(error) { switch (error.status) { case 401: // Re-authenticate break; case 403: showError('Insufficient permissions for this action.'); break; case 404: showError('The requested resource was not found.'); break; case 400: // Check endpoint docs for specific 400 response format showError('Bad request. Check the response body for details.'); break; case 422: showError('The request was valid but could not be processed.'); break; case 429: showError('Too many requests. Please wait before trying again.'); break; case 500: showError('Server error occurred. Please contact support.'); break; case 502: case 503: showError('Service temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.'); break; default: showError('An unexpected error occurred.'); } } ``` ## OpenAPI & Tools The complete OpenAPI specification (Swagger 2.0 format) provides programmatic access to our API documentation and can be imported into various development tools. **Download:** [OpenAPI Specification (JSON)](/swagger/v001/swagger.json) ### Use Cases - **Postman Collections** — Import directly into Postman for instant API testing - **Code Generation** — Generate client SDKs in your preferred language - **API Testing** — Import into testing tools like Insomnia or Paw - **Documentation** — Generate custom documentation for your team - **Validation** — Validate requests and responses against the schema ### Import into Postman **Step 1 — Open Postman:** - Launch the Postman application - Click "Import" in the top left corner **Step 2 — Import from URL (Recommended):** - Select the "Link" tab in the import dialog - Paste this URL: `https://api.pos.dutchie.com/swagger/v001/swagger.json` - Click "Continue" and then "Import" **Step 3 — Configure Authentication:** - Click on the imported collection name - Go to the "Authorization" tab - Select "Basic Auth" as the type - Enter your Location Key as the username - Enter your Integrator Key as the password (leave empty if you don't have one yet) - See the [Quick Start Guide](#description/quick-start-guide) for full authentication details **Step 4 — Test Your Setup:** - Find the `GET /whoami` request - Click "Send" to test your authentication - You should receive a 200 response with your location information > [!tip] > Your Postman collection is automatically generated from the live API and includes all current endpoints with proper authentication.

Returns product categories for your organization (e.g., Flower, Edibles,

Deleted categories are excluded. Organization-level, consistent across locations.

- [`GET /products`](#tag/product/GET/products) - Products reference these categories

tracking system (e.g., Metrc, BioTrack). Only items with non-zero differences

get.description:

Returns inventory transaction history — moves, adjustments, receives, converts,
combines, and more. Always use date filters for performance.

**Common Use Cases:**
- Reconciling inventory changes with external warehouse systems
- Auditing inventory movements for compliance reporting
- Building change logs for inventory dashboards

**Transaction types:** `Move`, `Convert`, `Adjust`, `Combine`, `Receive`,
`Change Product`, `Discontinue`, `Detail Update`, `Reconciliation`, `Create Package`

safety testing. Each result has `LabTest` (name), `Value`, `LabResultUnitId`,

- Displaying detailed COA (Certificate of Analysis) data on product pages

post.summary: Create or Update Batch Lab Results
post.description:
**Scope:** PackageWrite · **Rate Limit:** 120/min

Create or update cannabinoid and terpene lab results for a batch. All packages
within the batch share the same lab results. Only supports cannabinoid/terpene data —
safety testing (pesticides, heavy metals, etc.) is managed through separate workflows.

**Create vs Update:** If lab results already exist for the batch they are updated;
otherwise new results are created. Omitted analytes are preserved (sparse update).

**Create vs Update Behavior:**
- **CREATE**: When no lab results exist for the batch, new lab results will be created
- **UPDATE**: When lab results already exist for the batch, existing results will be updated
- **Validation**: Lab result data must pass validation requirements for regulatory compliance
- **Batch Sharing**: All packages within the same batch share identical lab results

**Request Body Fields:**
- `BatchName` (string, required): Name of the batch to update lab results for
- `SampleWeight` (decimal, optional): Weight of the sample tested in grams. Omit if sample weight was not recorded during testing.
- `LabResults` (array, required): Array of `CannabinoidTerpeneValue` objects containing test data
- `CoaUrl` (string, optional): URL to the Certificate of Analysis (COA) document. When provided, updates the stored COA URL. When omitted, existing COA URL is preserved.
- `LabName` (string, optional): Name of the laboratory that performed the testing. When omitted, existing value is preserved.
- `LabLicenseNumber` (string, optional): License number of the testing laboratory. When omitted, existing value is preserved.
- `TestedDate` (datetime, optional): Date the laboratory testing was performed. When omitted, existing value is preserved.

**CannabinoidTerpeneValue Structure:**
Each item in the `LabResults` array must contain:
- `LabResultName` (string, required): Name of the compound tested. Must be one of the valid cannabinoid or terpene names listed below.
- `Value` (decimal, required for most units): Measured concentration value of the compound. Must be null when unit is ND or LOQ.
- `LabResultUnitId` (int, required): Unit of measurement identifier:
  - `1` = Milligrams (mg) - requires numeric Value
  - `2` = Percentage (%) - requires numeric Value between 0-100
  - `3` = Milligrams per gram (mg/g) - requires numeric Value
  - `4` = ND (Not Detected) - Value must be null
  - `5` = LOQ (Limit of Quantitation) - Value must be null
  - `6` = Milligrams per serving (mg/serving) - requires numeric Value, commonly used for edibles

**Valid Cannabinoid Names:**
`THC`, `CBD`, `THCA`, `CBDA`, `CBC`, `CBG`, `CBGA`, `CBN`, `THCV`, `THC8`, `THC9`, `THC10`,
`CBDV`, `CBL`, `TAC`, `THCVA`, `CBDVA`, `CBLA`, `CBNA`, `CBCA`, `CBT`, `CBCV`, `TotalCannabinoids`

**Valid Terpene Names:**
`AlphaPinene`, `BetaPinene`, `BetaMyrcene`, `BetaCaryphyllene`, `TotalTerpenes`, `Fenchol`,
`GeraniolAcetate`, `Nerol`, `Sabinene`, `Terpineol`, `Valencene`, `Phytol`, `Terpinene`,
`ThreeCarene`, `Bisabolol`, `Guaiol`, `AlphaTerpinene`, `Camphene`, `Eucalyptol`, `Geraniol`,
`Isopulegol`, `Nerolidol`, `NerolidolTwo`, `OcimeneOne`, `OcimeneTwo`, `pCymene`,
`pIsopropyltouluene`, `Terpinolene`, `TransNerolidol`, `CaryophylleneOxide`, `BetaEudesmol`,
`Limonene`, `Humulene`, `Ocimene`, `Linalool`, `Farnesene`, `AlphaPhellandrene`, `YTerpinene`,
`Borneol`, `GammaTerpinene`, `DeltaThreeCarene`, `AlphaBisabolol`, `DeltaTerpinene`

**Related Endpoints:**
- `POST /package/lab-results` - Update lab results by package ID instead of batch name
- [`GET /inventory/labresults`](#tag/inventory/GET/inventory/labresults) - Retrieve lab results for display and verification
- [`GET /reference/lab-result-units`](#tag/referencedata/GET/reference/lab-result-units) - Get valid unit IDs and their meanings
- [`GET /reference/lab-results-names`](#tag/referencedata/GET/reference/lab-results-names) - Get valid analyte names programmatically

requestBody.description: Must include `BatchName` (identifies the batch) and `LabResults` array of `CannabinoidTerpeneValue` objects (each with `LabResultName`, `Value`, and `LabResultUnitId`). Optional: `SampleWeight` (grams) and `CoaUrl` (Certificate of Analysis link; omit to preserve existing).

200.description: Lab results created or updated. No response body.

400.description: Bad Request - String error message (parse response body as plain text) OR `ValidationResult` object with `isValid` boolean, `errors` array, and `ruleSetsExecuted` array

404.description: Not Found - Batch with specified name does not exist

requestBody.description: All fields required: `CustomerId`, `Subject`, `Body`, `Date`. Customer must exist and be accessible to your location.

Assigns one or more existing tags (by name) to a customer. Tags must already exist —
create them first via `POST /customer-tag`. Tags already assigned to the customer
are left unchanged.
            
**Related Endpoints:**
- [`POST /customer/remove-tags`](#tag/customer/POST/customer/remove-tags) - Remove specific tags

200.description: Tags successfully assigned.

post.description:
**Scope:** Customer · **Rate Limit:** 1500/min

Creates or updates a customer. Supports idempotency via `ConsumerKey` header
and `IdempotencyKey` field.

**Create vs Update:** Omit `CustomerId` (or set to 0) to create; provide it
to update. Creates include smart deduplication unless `bypassDeduplication=true`.

**Required for create:** `FirstName` (or `Name`), `Address1`, `City`, `State`,
`PostalCode`, `Status`, `CustomerType`. Updates are sparse — omitted fields
preserve existing values.

**Important:** `DateOfBirth` must be between 1800-01-01 and the current date.
Values outside this range will be rejected.

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`POST /customer/customerLookup`](#tag/customer/POST/customer/customerLookup) - Find existing customers first
- [`POST /customer/search`](#tag/customer/POST/customer/search) - Search by name, phone, email
- [`GET /customer/by-external-id`](#tag/customer/GET/customer/by-external-id) - Lookup by external ID

parameters.name: bypassDeduplication
parameters.description: Skip duplicate detection. Default: false.

parameters.name: ConsumerKey
parameters.description: GUID for idempotency (pair with `IdempotencyKey` in body).

requestBody.description: EcomCustomerEdit object. For create: required fields above. For update: `CustomerId` required, all others optional.

200.description: The saved Customer object with assigned ID and loyalty status.

400.description: `BadRequestResponse` — validation failed.

post.description:
**Scope:** Customer · **Rate Limit:** 1500/min

Finds exactly one customer using a prioritized search hierarchy:
1. EcomUserId, 2. MMJ ID, 3. Email, 4. Phone,
5. LastName + DateOfBirth, 6. FirstName + LastName.
Stops at the first match. If multiple match the same criterion, returns
the one with the lowest CustomerId.

**Important:** Fields are searched in priority order, not combined. Providing
both `EmailAddress` and `Phone` will only search by email (higher priority).

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`POST /customer/search`](#tag/customer/POST/customer/search) - Returns multiple matches with match types
- [`POST /customer/customer`](#tag/customer/POST/customer/customer) - Create/update after lookup
- [`GET /customer/by-external-id`](#tag/customer/GET/customer/by-external-id) - Lookup by external ID

parameters.name: includeSegments
parameters.description: Include segment data (internal use). Default: false.

requestBody.description: EcomCustomerEdit with search fields: `EcomUserId`, `MMJIDNumber`, `EmailAddress`, `Phone`, `FirstName`, `LastName`, `DateOfBirth`.

200.description: Single Customer object with loyalty status.

400.description: `BadRequestResponse` — invalid input.

404.description: No customer matches the search criteria.

Applies opt-in/opt-out changes for the supplied addresses. Each change is recorded in
the opt-in history audit trail (`Context = "PublicAPI"`), including the first-ever
opt-in for an address. Returns a per-item result (`updated`, `unchanged`, or `invalid`);
one bad row never fails the batch. Duplicate addresses are processed in order, last
write wins.

200.description: OK

400.description: Bad Request

Removes one or more tags (by name) from a customer. Tag names not currently assigned
to the customer are ignored.

- [`POST /customer/set-tags`](#tag/customer/POST/customer/set-tags) - Replace the full tag set

removed, and tags in the list not currently assigned are added. Tags must already exist —

post.description:
**Scope:** Deliveries · **Rate Limit:** 100/min

Updates route details for a delivery — assign drivers, vehicle, route notes,
and/or status. All fields except TransactionId are optional; only provided
fields are updated.

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`GET /Deliveries`](#tag/deliveries/GET/Deliveries) - View current delivery status
- [`GET /drivers`](#tag/drivers/GET/drivers) - Get valid driver IDs for assignment
- [`GET /preorder/Status`](#tag/preorder/GET/preorder/Status) - Pre-order info for delivery prep

requestBody.description: `TransactionId` (required) identifies the delivery. Optional: `DriverId`, `DriverId2`, `VehicleId`, `Route`, `Status`.

200.description: Route details updated. No response body.

400.description: `ValidationResult` — returned when request validation fails.

post.description:
**Scope:** CultivationWrite · **Rate Limit:** 120/min

Creates and/or updates multiple harvests in one request. Supports mixed
operations (some creates, some updates). Atomic — all succeed or all fail.
Validation runs before any operations execute.

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`GET /harvest`](#tag/harvest/GET/harvest) - View harvest records
- [`POST /harvest`](#tag/harvest/POST/harvest) - Single harvest create/update

requestBody.description: Contains a `Harvests` array. Omit `HarvestId` per item to create; provide it to update.

200.description: BulkCreateOrUpdateHarvestResponse with `CreatedHarvestIds` and `UpdatedHarvestIds` arrays.

400.description: `BadRequestResponse` — validation failed before any operations ran.

post.description:
**Scope:** Inventory · **Rate Limit:** 120/min

Creates a receive order for incoming inventory. Two modes:
- **Draft** (`ReceiveIntoInventory=false`): Saved for review/editing in Dutchie POS.
- **Direct** (`ReceiveIntoInventory=true`): Immediately processes into inventory
  (requires `UserId` or `UserName`, not both).

**Common Use Cases:**
- Automating vendor deliveries from purchase order or ERP systems
- Bulk receiving manifests from traceability systems

Validates vendor, room assignments, potency indicators, and `ExternalId`
uniqueness before processing.

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`GET /inventory/receivedinventory`](#tag/inventory/GET/inventory/receivedinventory) - View receive history
- [`GET /vendor/vendors`](#tag/vendor/GET/vendor/vendors) - Valid VendorId values
- [`GET /room/rooms`](#tag/room/GET/room/rooms) - Valid RoomId values

requestBody.description: Contains `Items` array (ProductId, Quantity, Cost, RoomId, PackageId, etc.), vendor info, and delivery details. `UserId` or `UserName` required when `ReceiveIntoInventory=true`.

200.description: SavedReceive with `ReceiveInventoryHistoryId`.

400.description: `BadRequestResponse` or plain text string — validation failed.

post.description:
**Scope:** PackageWrite · **Rate Limit:** 120/min

**Adds** tags to packages while preserving all existing tags. Duplicates
are silently ignored. Specify packages using either `InventoryIds` or
`PackageIds` (mutually exclusive).

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`POST /package/set-tags`](#tag/package/POST/package/set-tags) - Replace all tags
- [`POST /package/remove-tags`](#tag/package/POST/package/remove-tags) - Remove specific tags
- [`GET /tag`](#tag/tag/GET/tag) - Available tag names

requestBody.description: `Tags` (required) plus either `InventoryIds` or `PackageIds` (not both).

200.description: Success - Tags successfully added to specified packages

400.description: Bad Request - `ValidationResult` object with `isValid` boolean, `errors` array, and `ruleSetsExecuted` array

post.description:
**Scope:** PackageWrite · **Rate Limit:** 120/min

**Removes** specific tags from packages while preserving all other tags.
Removing a tag that doesn't exist is silently ignored. Specify packages
using either `InventoryIds` or `PackageIds` (mutually exclusive).

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`POST /package/set-tags`](#tag/package/POST/package/set-tags) - Replace all tags
- [`POST /package/add-tags`](#tag/package/POST/package/add-tags) - Add tags
- [`GET /tag`](#tag/tag/GET/tag) - Available tag names

requestBody.description: `Tags` to remove (required) plus either `InventoryIds` or `PackageIds` (not both).

200.description: Success - Tags successfully removed from specified packages

400.description: Bad Request - `ValidationResult` object with `isValid` boolean, `errors` array, and `ruleSetsExecuted` array

post.description:
**Scope:** PackageWrite · **Rate Limit:** 120/min

**Replaces** all existing tags on the specified packages with the provided tag set.
Specify packages using either `InventoryIds` or `PackageIds` (mutually exclusive — not both).

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`POST /package/add-tags`](#tag/package/POST/package/add-tags) - Add tags without removing existing ones
- [`POST /package/remove-tags`](#tag/package/POST/package/remove-tags) - Remove specific tags
- [`GET /tag`](#tag/tag/GET/tag) - Available tag names for validation

requestBody.description: `Tags` (required) plus either `InventoryIds` or `PackageIds` (not both).

200.description: Success - Tags successfully set on specified packages

400.description: Bad Request - `ValidationResult` object with `isValid` boolean, `errors` array, and `ruleSetsExecuted` array

post.description:
**Scope:** Inventory or Cultivation · **Rate Limit:** 120/min

Assigns existing plants to a plant group by serial number. The group must
already exist. Supports bulk assignment.

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`GET /plant`](#tag/plant/GET/plant) - View current group assignments
- [`POST /plant`](#tag/plant/POST/plant) - Create plants (auto-assigns to group)

requestBody.description: `PlantGroupName` (required, must exist), `PlantSerialNumbers` (required array).

200.description: Plants assigned. No response body.

400.description: `BadRequestResponse` — invalid serial numbers or group not found.

post.description:
**Scope:** CultivationWrite · **Rate Limit:** 120/min

Updates the cultivation growth phase for plants. Syncs with external
cultivation systems when configured.

**Valid phases:** `Propagation`, `Vegetative`, `Flowering`

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`GET /plant`](#tag/plant/GET/plant) - View current phases
- [`POST /plant/move`](#tag/plant/POST/plant/move) - Move between rooms
- [`POST /plant/harvest`](#tag/plant/POST/plant/harvest) - Harvest after flowering

requestBody.description: `PlantIds` (required), `GrowthPhase` (required: Propagation, Vegetative, or Flowering), `PhaseStartDate` (optional, defaults to now UTC).

200.description: Phase updated. No response body.

400.description: Invalid growth phase or validation error.

post.description:
**Scope:** CultivationWrite · **Rate Limit:** 300/min

Moves plants from Active to Harvesting status. Supports bulk operations
and optional wet weight tracking.

**Important:** Only plants in 'Active' status can be harvested. This is an
irreversible status change — harvested plants cannot return to Active.

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`GET /plant`](#tag/plant/GET/plant) - View current plant status
- [`POST /harvest`](#tag/harvest/POST/harvest) - Create harvest records
- [`GET /harvest`](#tag/harvest/GET/harvest) - Monitor harvest progress

requestBody.description: Plant IDs to harvest, `HarvestId`, and `HarvestedOn` date.

200.description: Plants moved to harvest status. No response body.

post.description:
**Scope:** CultivationWrite · **Rate Limit:** 120/min

Moves plants to a different room within the same facility. If the target
room has a cultivation stage configured, plants automatically update to
that stage. Syncs with external cultivation systems when configured.

**Important:** Cannot move plants between different facilities. The target
room must belong to the same LspId and LocId as the plants.

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`GET /plant`](#tag/plant/GET/plant) - Current plant locations
- [`POST /plant/change-phase`](#tag/plant/POST/plant/change-phase) - Update growth phase
- [`GET /room/rooms`](#tag/room/GET/room/rooms) - Available rooms

requestBody.description: `PlantIds` (required), `RoomId` (required, same facility), `TableId` (optional).

200.description: Plants moved. No response body.

400.description: Target room in different facility or validation error.

post.description:
**Scope:** CultivationWrite · **Rate Limit:** 300/min

Permanently retires plants from cultivation. Irreversible — retired plants
cannot be reactivated. Provide either `ReasonId` or `ReasonCode` (if both,
ReasonId takes precedence).

**Related Endpoints:**
- [`GET /plant`](#tag/plant/GET/plant) - View plant status before retirement
- [`GET /plant/get-reason-codes`](#tag/plant/GET/plant/get-reason-codes) - Valid reason codes
- [`POST /waste/PlantWaste`](#tag/waste/POST/waste/PlantWaste) - Create waste records for retired material

requestBody.description: `PlantIds` (required), `ReasonId` or `ReasonCode` (one required), `RoomId` (required). Optional: `WasteType`, `WasteWeight`, `PlantWeight`, `WasteDate`.

200.description: Plants retired. No response body.

400.description: `BadRequestResponse` — invalid reason or validation failed.

post.description:
**Scope:** PreOrder · **Rate Limit:** 240/min

post.summary: Look up email marketing opt-in status
post.description:
**Scope:** Customer · **Rate Limit:** 120/min
            
Returns the recorded email opt-in status for each supplied address. Every input
produces exactly one result row, in input order (duplicates included). Matching is
case-insensitive (inputs are trimmed and lowercased internally); each result echoes
back the original address exactly as sent.
            
`modifiedDateUtc: null` with `optInStatus: true` means no opt-out is on file — email
is opted-in by default. Invalid addresses return `optInStatus: null` and
`error: "invalid_email"` without failing the batch.
            
**Caveat:** `optInStatus: true` reflects recorded consent, not deliverability —
SendGrid-side suppressions (hard bounces, spam complaints) may still suppress delivery.

200.description: OK

400.description: Bad Request

post.summary: Look up SMS marketing opt-in status
post.description:
**Scope:** Customer · **Rate Limit:** 120/min
            
Returns the recorded SMS opt-in status for each supplied phone number. Every input
produces exactly one result row, in input order (duplicates included). Matching is by
cleaned digits internally, so differently-formatted inputs for the same number (e.g.
"(201) 669-0519" and "201-669-0519") return as separate rows resolving to the same
status; each result echoes back the original number exactly as sent.
            
`modifiedDateUtc: null` with `optInStatus: false` means no opt-in is on file — SMS is
opted-out by default. Invalid numbers return `optInStatus: null` and
`error: "invalid_phone"` without failing the batch.

200.description: OK

400.description: Bad Request

UpdateStrain.description:
Request model for creating or updating cannabis strain information.

**Create vs Update Behavior:**
- **CREATE**: Omit `StrainId` (or set to null) to create a new strain
- **UPDATE**: Provide an existing `StrainId` to update that strain

**Sparse Update Behavior:**
- **Provided fields**: Will overwrite existing values with provided data
- **Omitted fields**: Will preserve existing values (no data loss for updates)
- **Special handling**: `StrainDescription` is always required and cannot be null
